geometry_units: canvas pixels; angles in clockwise degrees; tangent variation is unwrapped angular range
curve_normalization: subtract start, rotate endpoint chord horizontal, divide by chord length, round to 0.001

labels.path_rationale: Caps the highest summit in its open northern sky; the unequal shoulders follow the peak silhouette without crossing it.
Begins beside the southern pass mouth and settles into the foothill shelf east of the tower.
Runs along the short canyon corridor between the western forest and central lowlands, clear of the provincial lettering below.
Hugs the southeast reservoir outlet, with a short rising lead and a restrained downstream turn.
A compact capital treatment beside the lower river, following the waterfront shelf rather than a regional arch.
Ends beside the western harbor anchor; the basin-shaped approach follows the coastal indentation.
Follows the upper edge of the port basin and eases around the coastal woodland instead of spreading across the province.
Follows the woodland's northeastward run, easing as the forest widens toward the lake; the modest turn keeps the lettering quiet within the trees.
Follows the asymmetric northwest-to-southeast lake spine, easing toward the outlet while keeping the letters within the basin.
A short reverse curve follows the bend of the Vaur below Zuidbrug, with lettering beside the channel rather than across the peninsula.
Follows the ascending pass approach and flattens at the saddle, distinguishing the pass from the tower below.
A long asymmetric crest-line sweep follows the change in bearing of the northern range; its letters clear the mountain tips.
Occupies the western mainland shoulder between woodland and mineral uplands, following the land mass into its southern hills.
Crosses the open central lowlands between the reservoir and capital; the name remains inland rather than naming the southern bay.
An inflected east-interior sweep follows the rolling country and stops before the coastal forest; all lettering belongs to Panterra.
A restrained national title occupies the northern margin, with an almost level individually drawn baseline separate from geographic regions.
Starts just east of the bridge town and follows the adjacent riverbank landing with a shallow downstream bend.
Ends beside the ancient western lakeshore city, following the reservoir-side woodland edge.
Starts beside the lower-river landing and carries the port name along the mouth-side terrace, below Heilig.
Sits immediately above the fortress site on the open northern shelf, with a compact bend around the foothill.
Tracks the active copper-valley floor below the western province name, distinct from the abandoned coastal mine.
Runs along the forest works edge near its anchor and avoids the wooded provincial corridor below.
Follows the diagonal approach to the abandoned lighthouse at the western peninsula tip.
A compact coastal-hill curve identifies the abandoned mine next to its original anchor, separate from Kupferdal.
Approaches the naval harbor from the sea and ends beside the waterfront anchor without labeling the offshore island.
Follows the southeast-facing harbor coast and opens into the sea, keeping the settlement attached to Panterra.
Wraps the east-facing shoulder of the southern island with a descending-then-level shoreline curve.
Sits above the inland high-valley city and lake, separate from the marine island and lower coastal town.
Follows the coastal river landing east of its anchor and the inside turn of the northern bay shore.
Spans the rolling wilderness along its changing hill crest, above the eastern province name.
Follows the concave upland saddle between the northern mountain foot and central hill country.
Crosses the old northern woodland following its upper edge, then turns with the forest toward the lake.
Follows the mineral foothills just inland of the southern bay, leaving the coast visible beneath the lettering.
Threads the western saddle near Oerkrone and bends below the high ridge, clearly apart from the Windnek passage.
Spans the open western sea basin, following its broad indentation and the southwest coastal bearing.
An open water sweep stays inside the sea between the two shores and changes direction with the long basin.
Runs with the upper-valley vineyard terrace below the dam and above the central provincial lettering.
A short riverbank curve sits beside the upper-valley town without crossing the Vaur label.
Names the active beacon above the northern edge of the western coastal spur; the full landmark name remains in the inventory.
Ends beside the ancient temple at the foot of the western mountains; concise monument lettering leaves the valley open.
Tracks the northern woodland entrance near the avian monument, avoiding the fortress and regional forest lettering.
